name: Chain-Link Fence
desc: A chain-link fence running away across the mid-ground — woven diamond mesh on line posts with a top rail and three barbed strands raked out overhead, a grey zip-tied sign, bindweed climbing through the wire and a caught bag working itself loose — while a swathe of light travels the fence and glints off every knuckle in the mesh.

energy.doc: wind in the vines and the bag, plus the strength of the sheen travelling the wire

scale.doc: fence height at the near end vs frame

density.doc: mesh gauge (how fine the diamonds are), post count and barb spacing

growth.doc: how much vegetation has come up through the wire

speed.doc: rate of the sheen travelling the fence, and of the wind

hue.doc: wire hue (204 = galvanised zinc; vegetation and rust always answer on the complement)

x.doc: anchor x for the fence line

y.doc: ground line at the near end — the fence recedes and rises from here

alpha.doc: opacity of the sheen, growth and bag — drop it to sit the fence back

style.doc: galvanised: bright new zinc wire, hard and municipal, every knuckle catching the travelling light · overgrown: nature taking it back — the mesh half-swallowed by climbing growth, no barbed wire left · slats: privacy slats threaded through the weave — colour-blocked and blank, but gapped and missing in places so the light still gets past · moire: two fences one behind the other, the meshes interfering into a slow drifting moire — pattern, not object · derelict: cut through and rusted out, whole panels of mesh torn away, dark and abandoned

act.doc: breeze: the vines and the bag work quietly · gale: weather — everything loose is snapping · still: dead air, the bag hangs, only the light moves

seed.doc: deterministic seed for mesh tone, torn panels, post spacing, growth and where the bag caught
